Subject: PO format + invoice cadence question for Redwood services

Hi Jonas,

Quick question from our procurement team — Crescent needs the following confirmed before we can issue a PO: 1) a PO header that includes our entity code (CH-001), 2) ability to handle bundled SKU line items (we map services to internal SKU bundles), and 3) whether Redwood can produce weekly consolidated invoices instead of monthly statements. Our ERP posts weekly and monthly batching causes reconciliation work.

Also, what net terms do you require to keep the pricing bands in Appendix A? Procurement typically enforces net60 for vendors and we need to understand any discount or packaging impact if we request net60 vs your standard net30.

Can you send a sample PO template and confirm which invoice line fields you need (PO number, project code, SKU mapping, tax/GL)? We may need to run this through our AP lead (cc'd).

Thanks,
Elena Alvarez
Sr. Procurement Manager
Crescent Health

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary from our side so procurement can review:

- Bundled SKUs: we support bundling (service SKU -> invoice line bundle). We ask that the PO enumerates bundle names and unit counts; internal SKU mapping column (we use "supplier_sku") helps our billing system map to the correct rate.

- Invoice cadence: we can issue weekly consolidated invoices (one invoice per week with line items grouped by bundle/project). Our standard is monthly, but weekly is feasible if you provide a billing contact and the ERP posting code per invoice (CH-001 as you noted).

- Net terms & discounts: our published pricing bands (Appendix A) assume net30. We can accommodate net60, but commercial impact depends on the discount band: for annual committed packages the effective discount reduces by ~1.5% if terms extend to net60 due to financing cost. For reference: Standard (net30): 18% volume discount at $250k ARR; Net60: same band requires either 1) a 12-month prepayment or 2) retain net30 discount and accept a small surcharge. We can walk numbers with your finance team.

I'll attach our PO template and a short mapping doc for invoice fields. If it's helpful, Marissa (AE) can propose a deal-level tradeoff (e.g., commit to a quarterly minimum to keep net30 pricing).

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood_PO_Template_v2.pdf (stub), SOW-Redwood-Crescent-v1.3.docx (stub)

We can escalate the SLA/credit discussion to procurement leadership if needed, but I wanted the basic tradeoffs so I can draft formal PO language.

Hi Elena — Marissa here (account lead). Two pragmatic pathways we typically use: 

Option A (preserve Appendix A discounts + net30): Crescent commits to a 12-month minimum ARR of $250k and provides CH-001 as the PO entity code. Billing remains weekly (if preferred) but invoiced amounts will apply toward the annual commitment. This keeps the 18% discount band intact.

Option B (accommodate net60): We can accept net60 with no prepayment if Crescent agrees to a 6-month rolling minimum of $150k ARR; in that case the published discount moves to 16% (a 2% reduction). We also add a small late-payment interest clause (0.5% monthly) to protect both parties.

Operational asks: please confirm your vendor setup timeline (when CH-001 will be active in your ERP) and provide the AP contact (name + email). Once we have that, Vanessa will produce a sample weekly invoice extract layout that matches your Excel mapping.

I'll mark up the attached PO template with the fields we need (supplier_sku, purchase_unit, bundle_name, project_code, PO_number, invoice_week_start).

If either option works, I can generate an acceptance amendment and routing instructions for your procurement portal.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Elena — ops & billing here. A few technical notes to make weekly consolidation smooth: 

- Required invoice fields: PO number, PO line, supplier_sku, bundle_name, quantity, unit_price, tax_amount, net_amount, invoice_week_start, invoice_week_end, CH-ERP-code.
- If you want weekly consolidated invoices, we will send one PDF per week and a CSV line-item extract for automated ingestion. We can include your GL code on each line if you provide the mapping.
- For vendor setup we need: registered vendor name, W-9 (or local equivalent), AP email, and vendor ACH details. If Crescent prefers ACH with net60, please note that our finance team will route payments through our bank partner and needs the vendor banking info up front.

I'll prepare the CSV column sample and share a short SFTP / secure upload spec if you'd like automated delivery.

Regards,
